meta.title: MCP Question Bank — Chapter 12: Transports & Protocol Utilities
meta.revision: v2.1 (curated 2026-09-12, 200 items, verified against the 2026-07-28 specification)

questions.question: A stdio server prints 'Listening for requests...' with print(). What breaks, and what is the fix?

options.text: The host discards the process; add the line to the config's ignore list
The server blocks until the client drains stdout; write asynchronously instead
The client cannot parse that line as a message; log to stderr instead
Nothing breaks, but the line is echoed into the model's context; use a log level

questions.explanation: The server MUST NOT write anything to stdout that is not a valid MCP message. Anything else corrupts framing. stderr is explicitly available for logging, and the client MAY capture, forward or ignore it.

questions.question: An SSE response stream dies halfway through a long tools/call. What must the client do in 2026-07-28?

options.text: Poll tasks/get with the original request id until the result appears
Reconnect and send Last-Event-ID to resume the stream where it broke
Open a GET stream to collect the messages buffered while it was away
Re-issue the request as a new request with a new JSON-RPC id

questions.explanation: Resumability and message redelivery were removed with the Last-Event-ID header and SSE event ids. A broken stream loses the in-flight request, and the client MUST re-issue it with a new id. tasks/get only applies if the Tasks extension created a task.

questions.question: A legacy client sends GET to a server that implements only 2026-07-28. What should the server return?

options.text: 405 Method Not Allowed, since the modern endpoint accepts POST only
400 Bad Request with an UnsupportedProtocolVersion error body
404 Not Found with a JSON-RPC -32601 Method not found body
200 with an SSE stream, for backwards compatibility with the GET endpoint

questions.explanation: The GET stream and DELETE session termination are gone: a modern-only server responds 405 to GET or DELETE, ignores Mcp-Session-Id, and ignores Last-Event-ID. 404 with -32601 is for an unknown JSON-RPC method on a POST.

questions.question: Which header must appear on EVERY Streamable HTTP POST, and what happens if its value disagrees with the body?

options.text: Mcp-Session-Id; a mismatch is rejected with 400 and InvalidRequest (-32600)
Mcp-Name; a mismatch is rejected with 400 and HeaderMismatch (-32020)
MCP-Protocol-Version; a mismatch is rejected with 400 and HeaderMismatch (-32020)
MCP-Protocol-Version; a mismatch is rejected with 400 and UnsupportedProtocolVersion (-32022)

questions.explanation: MCP-Protocol-Version is required on every POST and MUST equal the _meta protocol version; any header/body disagreement or missing required header is 400 + -32020. -32022 is different: the header and body agree, but the server does not support that version. Mcp-Name is required only for tools/call, resources/read and prompts/get.

questions.question: How does a client cancel an in-flight request, and why does it differ by transport?

options.text: HTTP: send DELETE to the MCP endpoint. stdio: close the server's stdin
Both: send notifications/cancelled, since cancellation is defined at the data layer
Both: close the connection, which the server must interpret as cancelling everything still in flight
HTTP: close that request's SSE stream. stdio: send notifications/cancelled with the request id

questions.explanation: On Streamable HTTP each request has its own response stream, so the transport-level disconnect is unambiguous and is itself the cancel signal. On stdio every message shares one channel, so the client sends notifications/cancelled referencing the request id.

questions.question: A gateway wants to route and rate-limit MCP traffic without parsing request bodies. Which header tells it the target, and on which requests does it appear?

options.text: Mcp-Method, on tools/call, resources/read and prompts/get only
Mcp-Name, on tools/call, resources/read and prompts/get
Mcp-Target, on any request that names a primitive in its params
Mcp-Name, on every request, alongside Mcp-Method

questions.explanation: Mcp-Method appears on all requests and names the JSON-RPC method; Mcp-Name names the specific primitive and is required only on the three methods that address one — tools/call, resources/read and prompts/get. Together they let infrastructure route without reading the body.
